faqs.q: The Directive Principles of State Policy are enumerated in the Constitution between which Articles?
The framers of the Indian Constitution borrowed the concept of Directive Principles from which Constitution?
The Irish Constitution of 1937 had itself borrowed the concept of Directive Principles from which Constitution?
Who described the Directive Principles as 'novel features' of the Indian Constitution?
Who described the Directive Principles and Fundamental Rights together as the 'Conscience of the Constitution'?
Under Article 36, the term 'State' in Part IV has the same meaning as in which Part?
The Directive Principles resemble the 'Instrument of Instructions' found in which enactment?
The Directive Principles embody the concept of a welfare state as opposed to which concept?
Which Article declares that the Directive Principles are fundamental in governance and it is the State's duty to apply them?
A law giving effect to a Directive Principle may be treated as 'reasonable' in relation to which two Articles?
Which of the following is NOT a category of Directive Principles?
Which Article directs the State to minimise inequalities in income, status, facilities and opportunities?
faqs.e: This specific provision on minimising inequalities was added to Article 38 by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.

faqs.q: Which Article directs the State to secure adequate means of livelihood for all citizens?
Which Article directs the State to secure equal pay for equal work for men and women?
Article 39 directs the State to prevent concentration of which of the following?
faqs.e: Article 39's provision protecting children and youth from exploitation and moral abandonment was added later by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

faqs.q: Which Article provides for equal justice and free legal aid to the poor?
faqs.e: Article 39A was inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

faqs.q: Which Article directs the State to secure the right to work, education, and public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement?
Which Article provides for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief?
Which Article directs the State to secure a living wage and decent standard of life for workers?
A 'living wage' differs from a 'minimum wage' mainly by additionally covering which of the following?
Which Article directs the State to secure participation of workers in the management of industries?
Which Article directs the State to raise the level of nutrition, standard of living, and public health?
Which Article directs the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government?
Which Article directs the State to promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas?
Which Article directs the State to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, and democratic control of co-operative societies?
faqs.e: Article 43B was inserted by the 97th Amendment Act, 2011.

faqs.q: Which Article directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs, and other weaker sections?
Which Article directs the State to prohibit the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs injurious to health?
Which Article directs the State to prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves, and other milch and draught cattle?
Which Article directs the State to secure a uniform civil code for all citizens?
Which Article provides for early childhood care and education for children until the age of six years?
faqs.e: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 changed Article 45's subject matter; it originally provided for free and compulsory education up to age 14, which is now a Fundamental Right under Article 21A.

faqs.q: Which Article directs the State to organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines?
Which Article directs the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife?
faqs.e: Article 48A was inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

faqs.q: Which Article directs the State to protect monuments, places and objects of national importance?
Which Article directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services?
Which Article directs the State to promote international peace and security and to encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration?
Before the 86th Amendment, Article 45 provided free and compulsory education for children up to what age?

Consider the following Directive Principles:
(I) Securing opportunities for healthy development of children (Article 39)
(II) Providing free legal aid to the poor (Article 39A)
(III) Securing participation of workers in management of industries (Article 43A)
Which of the above were added as new Directive Principles by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976?
faqs.e: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added four new Directive Principles: Article 39 (healthy development of children), Article 39A (free legal aid), Article 43A (worker participation in industry management), and Article 48A (environment and wildlife protection).

faqs.q: Who recommended dividing individual rights into justiciable and non-justiciable categories?
faqs.e: Sir B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly. Following his recommendation, justiciable rights were placed in Part III (Fundamental Rights) and non-justiciable rights in Part IV (Directive Principles).

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the distinction between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles:
(I) Fundamental Rights are negative in nature while Directive Principles are positive
(II) Fundamental Rights are justiciable while Directive Principles are non-justiciable
(III) Fundamental Rights require legislation for implementation while Directive Principles are automatically enforced
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: Statement III is reversed — Fundamental Rights do not require legislation and are automatically enforced, while Directive Principles require legislation and are not automatically enforced.

faqs.q: Fundamental Rights aim at establishing which type of democracy, while Directive Principles aim at establishing social and economic democracy?
Which of the following correctly describes the sanction behind Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles respectively?

options.b: Fundamental Rights have moral sanctions; Directive Principles have legal sanctions
options.d: Fundamental Rights have legal sanctions; Directive Principles have moral and political sanctions

faqs.a: Fundamental Rights have legal sanctions; Directive Principles have moral and political sanctions

faqs.q: If a law is found violative of a Directive Principle, what can the courts do?

options.a: Cannot declare it unconstitutional, though they can uphold a law enacted to give effect to a directive

faqs.a: Cannot declare it unconstitutional, though they can uphold a law enacted to give effect to a directive

faqs.q: Who dubbed the Directive Principles as 'pious superfluities' and compared them to a cheque payable only when the bank's resources permit?
Which critic described the Directive Principles as 'a veritable dustbin of sentiments'?

Who remarked that Part IV of the Constitution "expresses Fabian Socialism without the socialism," criticising the Directive Principles as conservative and rooted in 19th century English political philosophy?
K. Santhanam criticised the Directive Principles on the ground that they could lead to constitutional conflict between which of the following pairs?
faqs.e: K. Santhanam pointed to potential conflict between the Centre and the states, between the President and the Prime Minister, and between the Governor and the Chief Minister over implementation of the Directive Principles.

faqs.q: Who compared the Directive Principles to 'new year's resolutions, which are broken on the second of January'?
Which critic held the view that the Directive Principles are 'neither properly classified nor logically arranged', mixing unimportant issues with vital economic and social questions?
Who described the Directive Principles as the 'life giving provisions of the Constitution' that constitute the stuff of the Constitution and its philosophy of social justice?
Which former Chief Justice of India remarked that if all the Directive Principles were fully carried out, the country would be a "heaven on earth"?
Ambedkar pointed out the Directive Principles lay down the goal of Indian polity as which of the following, as distinguished from political democracy?
Granville Austin opined that the Directive Principles are aimed at furthering the goals of which of the following?
According to Setalvad, Directive Principles serve as beacon-lights to courts in exercising which power?
In the Champakam Dorairajan case (1951), the Supreme Court ruled that in case of conflict between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles, which would prevail?
faqs.e: The Court held that Directive Principles must conform to and run as subsidiary to Fundamental Rights, but Fundamental Rights could be amended by Parliament through constitutional amendment acts. Following this ruling, Parliament made the 1st, 4th, and 17th Amendment Acts to implement some of the Directive Principles.

faqs.q: In the Golaknath case (1967), the Supreme Court ruled that Parliament cannot take away or abridge Fundamental Rights because they are of which nature?
Which Amendment Act declared that Parliament has the power to abridge or take away any Fundamental Right by enacting Constitutional Amendment Acts, in reaction to the Golaknath judgment?
The 25th Amendment Act, 1971 inserted which new Article into the Constitution?
faqs.e: As originally inserted, Article 31C protected laws implementing the Directive Principles specified in Article 39(b) and (c).

faqs.q: In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court declared which provision of Article 31C unconstitutional?

options.a: The provision extending protection to all Directive Principles
options.c: The provision barring courts from questioning laws that claim to give effect to Article 39
options.d: The provision immunising laws from Article 14 and 19 challenges

faqs.a: The provision barring courts from questioning laws that claim to give effect to Article 39
faqs.e: The Court held this second provision unconstitutional on the ground that judicial review is a basic feature of the Constitution. However, the first provision of Article 31C was upheld as valid.

faqs.q: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 extended the protection of Article 31C to cover laws implementing which of the following?
faqs.e: This extension, which accorded legal primacy to Directive Principles over Fundamental Rights, was declared unconstitutional in the Minerva Mills case (1980). The Minerva Mills ruling restored the subordination of Directive Principles to Fundamental Rights, though Fundamental Rights under Articles 14 and 19 remained subordinate specifically to Article 39(b) and (c).

faqs.q: Article 31 (right to property) was omitted from the Constitution by which Amendment Act?
In the Minerva Mills case (1980), the Supreme Court described Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles as being like which of the following?
As per the present constitutional position after the Minerva Mills case, which of the following holds true?

options.a: Parliament alone decides supremacy case by case
options.b: Fundamental Rights enjoy supremacy over Directive Principles
options.c: Both are equal and cannot be balanced
options.d: Directive Principles enjoy supremacy over Fundamental Rights

faqs.a: Fundamental Rights enjoy supremacy over Directive Principles
faqs.e: Even so, Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights to implement Directive Principles, provided the amendment does not damage or destroy the basic structure of the Constitution.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Golaknath case (1967):
(I) It was a Supreme Court judgment
(II) It held that the Fundamental Rights are sacrosanct
(III) It held that Parliament could amend Fundamental Rights to implement Directive Principles
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: The Golaknath judgment held the opposite of statement III — that Fundamental Rights could NOT be amended for implementing Directive Principles. This position was later reversed by the 24th Amendment Act.

faqs.q: Which body was established in 1950 to take up the planned development of the country, and was later replaced by NITI Aayog?
faqs.e: The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.

faqs.q: Which Act established a nation-wide network to provide free legal aid to the poor and to organise lok adalats?
Lok adalat, as a statutory forum for conciliatory settlement of disputes, has been given the status of which of the following?
faqs.e: Lok adalat awards are enforceable, binding on the parties, and final, with no appeal lying before any court against them.

faqs.q: Which Amendment Act provided constitutional status and protection to the three-tier panchayati raj system?
The 65th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1990 established which commission to protect the interests of SCs and STs?

options.d: National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes

faqs.a: National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
faqs.e: This combined commission was later bifurcated into two separate bodies — the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes — by the 89th Amendment Act, 2003.

faqs.q: Which Amendment Act conferred constitutional status on the National Commission for Backward Classes?
The 103rd Amendment Act, 2019 facilitated reservation for which category?
faqs.e: This Amendment enabled 10% reservation in admissions to educational institutions and civil posts for EWS persons not already covered under existing SC/ST/OBC reservation schemes.

faqs.q: Which Code separated the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the state, taking away judicial powers from executive authorities like the collector and tehsildar?
Which Act was enacted to protect monuments, places and objects of national importance?

options.b: Ancient and Historical Monument and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1951

faqs.a: Ancient and Historical Monument and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1951

faqs.q: Which Article, found outside Part IV, requires consideration of the claims of SCs and STs in making appointments to services and posts?
faqs.e: Article 335 is located in Part XVI of the Constitution and, though non-justiciable like other Directive Principles, is given equal importance by the judiciary.

faqs.q: Which Article, located in Part XVII, directs states to provide instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to children of linguistic minority groups?
Which Article places a duty on the Union to promote the spread and development of the Hindi language?
